title: Undo and recover from git mistakes
when: The user committed the wrong thing, lost work, committed to the wrong branch, or wants to undo a pushed change.
inputs: whether the commits were already pushed or shared
prompt:
Goal: The safest command for the situation, preserving work, with shared history rewritten only when it is safe.
Steps:
1. Ask or infer whether the commit was pushed: shared commits are undone with git revert, local ones may be rewritten.
2. Last local commit message or files wrong: fix and run git commit --amend.
3. Undo the last local commit but keep changes: git reset --soft HEAD~1; discard uncommitted edits to one file: git restore <file>.
4. Committed to the wrong branch: create the right branch at HEAD, then move the old branch back with git reset --keep HEAD~1.
5. Lost commits after a reset or rebase: find them with git reflog and restore with git branch rescue <hash>.
6. Before anything destructive, save a safety point: git branch backup-before-fix.
Quality bar:
- Each command is explained before it is run.
- Shared history is never force pushed without agreement.
- Work is backed up first.
Pitfalls:
- git reset --hard with uncommitted work.
- Force pushing over teammates commits.
- Reverting a merge without -m.
Verify:
- [ ] The situation is identified (pushed or local).
- [ ] A backup branch is created before risky steps.
- [ ] The final git log matches the goal.
- [ ] No placeholder text.
Output: The exact commands in order with one line explanations.

examples.input: commitei na branch errada, como desfaço?
examples.output: git branch feat/report, git reset --keep HEAD~1 on main, git switch feat/report
